title: Ibn al-Haytham: Master of Light
passage:
Ibn al-Haytham, known in Europe as Alhazen, was born in Basra around the year 965. As a young man, he studied math, the stars and philosophy, and he became known as a very talented scholar.

According to a famous story, the ruler of Egypt invited him to Cairo to find a way to control the flooding of the Nile River. After examining the river carefully, Ibn al-Haytham concluded that the project was impossible with the tools available at that time. Some historians say he then spent several years living quietly in Cairo, where he devoted himself to research and writing.

His most important work, the Book of Optics, changed how people understood light and sight. Many earlier thinkers believed that the eyes sent out rays that touched the objects we see. Ibn al-Haytham argued instead that light travels from objects into the eye. To support his ideas, he performed careful experiments with dark rooms, small openings and lamps, and he described how an image passes through a tiny hole.

More importantly, he insisted that scientists should test ideas through observation and experiment rather than simply accept the opinions of famous authorities. For this reason, many historians consider him an early pioneer of the scientific method.

He died around 1040. Later, his books were put into Latin, and they shaped the work of European scientists for many years.

questions.stem: Which word belongs to the same word family as 'observe'?
options: obvious
observation
service
obtain
questions.why: 'Observation' is the noun form of the verb 'observe'.

options: Test every idea with an experiment.
How does light enter the eye?
What a brilliant scholar he was!
Ibn al-Haytham was born in Basra.

questions.stem: What type of text is this passage?
options: A biography
A fable
A poem
A diary
questions.why: It tells the true story of a real person's life, from birth to death.

questions.stem: Which event happened FIRST in Ibn al-Haytham's life?
options: He traveled to Cairo in Egypt
He wrote the Book of Optics
He studied math and philosophy
His books were put into Latin
questions.why: He studied 'as a young man,' before the invitation to Cairo.

questions.stem: How did Ibn al-Haytham's idea about vision differ from earlier thinkers' ideas?
options: He said light enters the eye from objects
He said the eyes send rays to objects
He said vision does not need light
He said only lamps can be seen clearly
questions.why: Earlier thinkers believed the eyes sent out rays; he argued that light travels from objects into the eye.

questions.stem: The writer says his book 'changed how people understood light and sight.' What does this show?
options: The book was hard and unpopular
The book had a very large influence
The book was mainly about the Nile
The book was lost for many years
questions.why: The phrase shows how important and powerful the book was.

questions.stem: Which opinion is BEST supported by the passage?
options: He failed because he could not control the Nile
Only his early studies in Basra really mattered
Famous authorities are always correct
His experiments make him an important scientist
questions.why: Historians call him an early pioneer of the scientific method because he tested ideas by experiment.

questions.stem: Which information in the passage is LEAST certain?
options: Where Ibn al-Haytham was born
What the Book of Optics was about
Whether the Nile story is fully true
Which language his books were put into
questions.why: The writer calls it 'a famous story' and says only 'some historians' describe what followed.

questions.stem: Which event could really happen in a modern classroom?
options: Students form an image of a lamp through a tiny hole
Students see objects in a room with no light
A student's eyes send rays that light up a room
A lamp forms an image through a solid wall
questions.why: The passage describes how an image passes through a tiny hole, which really works.

questions.stem: Which is the BEST alternative title for the passage?
options: The Great Flood of the Nile
The Scholar Who Tested Light
A Journey to Basra
The Lamps of Cairo
questions.why: It focuses on his life and his experiments with light.
